description: Fixed 15-drug panel for the ESBL/MDR E. coli UTI MVP scope. Each drug is mapped either directly onto reaction(s) of a genome-scale metabolic model (simulation_mode='direct') or flagged as outside metabolic-model scope (simulation_mode='non_metabolic') when its target (ribosome, DNA gyrase, RNA polymerase, or a non-metabolic activation pathway) is not represented as a gene/reaction in the reconstruction. Non-metabolic drugs still appear in the panel and get literature/rule-based reasoning, but no FBA growth curve.

drugs.notes: First committed step of peptidoglycan precursor synthesis; essential in silico.
Model carries an isozyme (folM/b1606) with weak promiscuous activity, mirroring real trimethoprim biology where FolM gives low-level, clinically minor backup activity.
Sequential blockade partner for trimethoprim in the same pathway (co-trimoxazole); classic literature-validated synergy pair, useful as an internal sanity check for the Bliss/FIC math.

Beta-lactam subclasses share this reaction set in the model (GEMs do not resolve PBP-binding-affinity differences); subclasses are differentiated mainly through the resistance overlay (beta-lactamase hydrolysis profiles), not the baseline target.
Tazobactam's beta-lactamase inhibition is represented in the resistance overlay (it blunts, not eliminates, ESBL hydrolysis of the partner drug).
Prototypical ESBL substrate; strongly hydrolysed by CTX-M-15 in the resistance overlay.
ESBL substrate, hydrolysed similarly to ceftriaxone in the resistance overlay.
Stable to ESBL hydrolysis in the overlay; only carbapenemases (e.g. KPC) degrade it.
More ESBL/porin-loss susceptible than meropenem in practice; overlay gives it partial (not full) protection against ESBL.

Colistin's real target is mature LPS on the outer membrane, not LpxC catalysis directly; using the lipid A pathway as a proxy captures the same essential-pathway dependency and gives a graded dose-response, but is a simplification worth flagging.

drugs.target_enzyme: Nitroreductases (activate prodrug to multi-target reactive intermediates)
drugs.pathway: not represented as a discrete metabolic reaction in this reconstruction
drugs.notes: Damages ribosomes, DNA and multiple enzymes simultaneously once activated; this multi-target mechanism is outside what a stoichiometric GEM can represent.
DNA gyrase is not a metabolic enzyme and has no gene entry in iJO1366; confirmed absent from the loaded model.
Same target class as ciprofloxacin; not FBA-simulable in this model.
Ribosomal protein genes are absent from the metabolic reconstruction; translation is modeled only as a lumped biomass precursor demand.
Same class as gentamicin; not FBA-simulable in this model.
